notes: T862 (one dispatch path) — findings. DIRECTIVE D085 (amend, from orcha, acked 2026-08-24): tested whether apparent protocol non-compliance is a model failure or a harness artefact. RESULT (regression arm H, on the REAL verify_dispatch code path, same model/task/row/deliverable): the nonce check (`nonce in stdout`, tools/dispatch_verify.py:959) is INVOCATION-CONFOUNDED — a JSON-mode lane (--mode json) echoes the prompt (which carries the nonce) back to stdout, so the nonce appears whether or not the model wrote it; a non-JSON lane's stdout is only the model's reply. Measured: JSON-echo stdout (prompt + empty model reply) -> verification PASSED (exit 0); non-JSON stdout (bare 'done', no echo) -> verification FAILED: nonce echo missing (exit 2) — identical model behaviour, the verdict differs by invocation. CONCLUSION: 'unreliable protocol compliance' measured by the nonce check alone is a function of the HARNESS, not just the model; the planned eight-model compliance race MUST gate its invocation (same --mode json/--session flags for every lane, or a nonce channel independent of the prompt echo) before attributing non-compliance to a model — four recorded instances against one model are a false attribution until the invocation is equalised. The confound does NOT touch this task's defect-2 fix (the auto-close net) — it is about the nonce VERIFICATION channel, separate from the close. SCOPE: defect 2 (the auto-close safety net) fixed in tools/runner; defect 1's runner-side handle declaration verified; defect 1's lane-CONSTRUCTION fix (attaching --session/--mode json to the pi/openrouter lane) lives in bin/subagent, which is NOT in this task's declared deliverables (holds=bin/dispatch tools/runner tools/regression-one-dispatch-path.sh) — recorded as follow-up, not done here. RED BEFORE (measured): the runner's auto-done block was gated on `if ret == 0 and args.task_id:`; lanes dispatched via bin/subagent carry identity on MANAGENT_TASK_ID with --arbiter-id (no --task-id), so args.task_id is None and the net NEVER FIRED — a worker that exited 0 without closing left its row open with NO log line explaining why (40+ hand-closes in one day; the cited case: 1325 s of work, a 27743-byte deliverable committed, exit 0, row stayed open). For defect 1, two of four lanes received no session/transcript handle: deepseek and ollama get `--session <path>` (measurable); the pi/openrouter lane `pi --provider openrouter --model stealth/ox-alpha -p ...` has NO --session and NO --mode json; the claude lane `claude -p ... --output-format json` carries its transcript in a different envelope shape. GREEN AFTER (tools/runner, verified by tools/regression-one-dispatch-path.sh, all 8 arms PASS): (1) one identity resolution — the net uses the single resolved `task_identity` (--task-id OR MANAGENT_TASK_ID), not the raw --task-id flag; bin/dispatch stamps MANAGENT_TASK_ID at the detach door so the identity flows from one source. (2) the net closes on EVIDENCE — exit 0 plus every declared deliverable present on the filesystem — and calls `managent done` with a --note recording the close was automatic and the worker reported nothing, and --impression-waiver naming the reason. (3) the net REFUSES to close when a declared deliverable is absent: it logs `auto-close net: DECLINED — <task> exited 0 but declared deliverable(s) absent: <files>; row left open for a human (T862 §3 — missing evidence is a real failure, not a protocol slip)` and does NOT call done (control arm B proves this). (4) the net says so when it declines — no silent skip: when the row is already done (the worker closed — `not needed`), not in_progress, not in the store, or managent done itself refuses (claim-at-close T390, deliverable-not-committed, absorption gate), a log line states the reason; a degraded run (no identity) logs `auto-close net: declined — no task identity ... no row to close`. (5) no fabrication: the closed row's store record carries impression_waiver (named) and NO impression, and a verdict_note that records the close was automatic (control arm C proves this). VERDICT TENSION (recorded, not resolved): managent has no closed-but-unverified status, and this task cannot add one (src/managent/main.zig is serial-held by T485/486/487/497). The net records verdict=pass — the managent default — on the OBSERVED process evidence (exit 0 + declared deliverables present), attributed to the harness in --note, NOT as a worker-reported verdict; the impression is waived by name. If a stricter close-semantic is wanted (a verdict the runner did not 'observe' vs one it inferred from exit-0+deliverables), it needs a managent-side change (a new status or an auto-close provenance field), which is out of scope here. PROTOCOL NON-COMPLIANCE (brief §5): a worker that finishes correctly but skips the nonce and the close is a protocol datum belonging in the model record, not a work failure — the auto-close net closes the ROW (kanban accuracy) while the --note flags the worker reported nothing; the model-perf ledger is not mutated by the net, and per the D085 finding above, nonce-based compliance attribution must be invocation-gated before it is written against a model. FOUR LANES (exit + behaviour, after): all four lanes reach the runner via bin/subagent with --arbiter-id + MANAGENT_TASK_ID, so the net now fires for every lane on exit 0 (the defect-2 fix is lane-uniform). Session handle (defect 1): deepseek/ollama get --session (handle); pi/openrouter and claude do not — the runner records session_path for the --session lanes and a stated session_reason (declared unmeasurable) for the no-session lanes, never a blank cell (regression arm F). The remaining defect-1 work — attaching --session + --mode json to the pi/openrouter lane, and adapting the claude transcript envelope — is in bin/subagent and is the recommended follow-up; the D085 confound shows the nonce channel also needs equalising across lanes. REGRESSION: tools/regression-one-dispatch-path.sh, wired into zig build test (build.zig), 8 arms (A net-closes, B refuse-on-missing, C no-fabrication, D not-needed, E degraded, F lane-handle, G isolation, H D085-confound), runs in a scratch repo under /tmp/weizigo (no live-store leakage). NOT TEST-FIRST for defect 2: the bug could not be re-observed failing without reverting the gate (the old `args.task_id` block is replaced, not toggleable); the regression asserts the GREEN invariant plus the two controls (refuse-on-missing, no-fabrication) per the standing tooling rule's 'assert the invariant instead' clause.
